record.question: In a conventional PAP smear, what indicates an adequate specimen?
options: Presence of endocervical/ transformation zone component
record.explanation: Official final key: A — Presence of endocervical/ transformation zone component. MPSC notification 9 March 2026, Group B non-gazetted technical H&FW examination held 29 January–2 February 2026; key physical page 7, printed Q92. Source limitation: The offered “presence of endocervical/transformation zone component” is not a necessary adequacy criterion under current Bethesda practice; high cellularity alone is also not a sufficient complete adequacy definition. The final key establishes the historical marking choice without removing that limitation.
